top_buys.pitch: Refiners keep capturing fat margins as jet fuel and product prices climb.
top_buys.why: Reporting says airlines are cutting capacity specifically because jet fuel prices keep rising, and holiday airfares are up 23% — classic signs of tight refined-product markets. Valero is the purest large-cap play on crack spreads, and momentum screens already flag it as a leader. Middle East supply risk, including a fire near an Aramco facility in Riyadh, adds another leg to the tightness.
top_buys.risks: A ceasefire or demand slump would compress crack spreads fast, and refiners are volatile with big single-day swings.
top_buys.watch: Weekly EIA product inventory data and Q3 earnings in late October.

top_buys.pitch: Higher fares won't save airline profits when jet fuel keeps rising.
top_buys.why: CNBC explicitly reports that airfares can rise further but airline profits won't, because fuel costs are eating the gains and carriers are trimming capacity. Southwest has less international premium mix to offset fuel than the legacy carriers and no fuel hedging advantage anymore. The market has focused on fare headlines rather than the margin squeeze underneath.
top_buys.risks: If crude retreats on any Iran de-escalation, airline stocks would bounce hard and quickly.
top_buys.watch: Jet fuel crack spreads and Q3 airline earnings guidance later this month.

top_buys.pitch: Long bonds stay under pressure with yields near 5.3% and corporate supply surging.
top_buys.why: The 10-year is holding near 5.3% even as stocks rally, and commentary notes each new leg down in bonds pressures equities. Paramount's $52B debt sale shows how much new corporate paper is competing for the same buyers. My rate calls have been the most consistently right part of my record.
top_buys.risks: A soft inflation print or weak jobs data could spark a sharp bond rally, as the recent weak jobs report hinted.
top_buys.watch: The next CPI release and Treasury auction demand.

top_buys.pitch: A $5.7B oil sands bolt-on at a moment when crude supply risk is elevated.
top_buys.why: Cenovus is acquiring Athabasca Oil in cash and stock, adding long-life oil sands barrels with low decline rates. Acquirer shares often sag on announcement day then recover as investors digest the free-cash-flow accretion. With Middle East conflict keeping supply tight, Canadian heavy producers get an extra tailwind.
top_buys.risks: Investors may dislike the price or the share issuance, and a drop in crude would undercut the whole thesis.
top_buys.watch: Shareholder and regulatory approval timeline, and WCS differentials.

top_buys.pitch: A $945M bolt-on in radiopharma gives a lagging healthcare name a growth angle.
top_buys.why: GE HealthCare is acquiring Sofie Biosciences, deepening its molecular imaging and radiopharmaceutical capability — one of the faster-growing corners of diagnostics. Health Care was the worst sector last week (-2.2%), so expectations are low and a credible growth story can get rerated. Deal size is manageable relative to GEHC's balance sheet.
top_buys.risks: Healthcare remains out of favor and the deal is too small to move numbers much near term.
top_buys.watch: Any commentary on deal accretion at Q3 earnings.
